title: Zabaglione
subtitle: Warm Italian egg and Marsala custard
excerpt: Zabaglione is a warm, foamy custard made from egg yolks, sugar, and Marsala wine, whisked over gentle heat until it triples in volume. It is one of the fastest desserts in Italian cooking -- ready in under ten minutes from start to serve. Pour it into glasses and bring it straight to the table while it is still warm.
sourceNotes: Zabaglione (called zabaione in some regions) dates to at least the sixteenth century and appears in early recipe manuscripts from Turin. It is the ancestor of several other foamy custard desserts across Europe.

content.text: The bowl must not touch the simmering water below. Steam heat, not direct heat, gives a smooth zabaglione without scrambled egg.

items.prepNote: use Marsala wine -- or use dry sherry
serve warm in glasses, with savoiardi on the side if you like

content.text: Half-fill a saucepan with water and bring to a gentle simmer. Set a heatproof bowl over the top without touching the water.
Put the egg yolks and sugar in the bowl. Whisk briefly to combine.
Add the Marsala. Whisk continuously over the steam for 8-10 minutes. The mixture should triple in volume and become thick and pale.
The zabaglione is ready when the whisk leaves a ribbon trail that holds for a few seconds.
Pour immediately into warmed glasses and serve at once, with savoiardi on the side if you like.

items.symptom: The zabaglione has curdled into scrambled egg
items.cause: The heat was too high, or the bowl was touching the boiling water.
items.fix: Keep the water at a gentle simmer, not a boil. The bowl must hover above the water. If it starts to look grainy, remove from the heat immediately and whisk vigorously off the heat.

items.symptom: The mixture is not thickening after 10 minutes of whisking
items.cause: The bowl is too far from the heat, or the water is not hot enough.
items.fix: Increase the simmer very slightly. The bowl should feel very warm to the touch. Keep whisking -- it can take a few extra minutes on a cooler day.

items.cause: It sat too long before being poured.
items.fix: Pour and serve the moment it is ready. Zabaglione waits for no one -- have your glasses warm and your guests at the table before you start.

content.text: Zabaglione is a Piedmontese and Venetian classic with roots going back centuries. It appears in old cookbooks as both a dessert and a restorative drink. Today it is served in elegant trattorie as a simple finale to long lunches. The whole dish depends on technique, not ingredients.
